order: ORD-0295 addendum 2: red-team pass over the Q43 coordinate ruler r2 (a7e1d2d9740153918ad0906a4e913ffe81364eaf, selftest 9/9)

bites.expected: this IS a constant value claim; it must be judged
bites.why: CONSTANT_CLAIM regex matches ASCII '=' only; a fullwidth equals sign makes the claim invisible to F1 entirely
bites.severity: real hole - a writer who formats with a fullwidth '=' escapes the gate
bites.fix: normalize U+FF1D to '=' before scanning (or add ＝ to the = class)

bites.why: \d in Python matches unicode digits by default, so fullwidth digits ARE caught - good; recording as a verified strength, not a bite

bites.vector: "the lane said the deadline is 10000" / "据 F 的普查：写腿 14 处"
bites.why: RELAY_WORDS covers 10 phrases but NOT 'the lane said', '据 <name>', '转述', 'reportedly', 'per <lane>' - any relay phrasing outside the list escapes F2 entirely
bites.severity: real hole - relay wording is the easiest thing in the world to rephrase; a fixed phrase list cannot chase it
bites.fix: either grow the list continuously (losing race) or invert: flag any sentence containing a number + a comparative/attribution STRUCTURE (e.g. 不在本仓库的代词 + 数字), or require every relayed number to carry a coordinate regardless of wording (hardest, most mechanical)

bites.why: CONSTANT_CLAIM needs [A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{4,} = 5+ total chars; 4-letter names escape. 5-letter (SPEED = 80) is caught (measured RED).
bites.severity: known narrowness; the F1 family was scoped to named constants - a 4-letter constant with a forwarded value is a real escape but arguably rare in receipts

bites.class: attribution hole (BIT) - the commander's md:line+decoy case
bites.vector: claim with an unstable md:line coordinate AND an unrelated 40-hex within 200 chars
bites.expected (strict): RED - the md:line is unstable and the 40-hex coordinates a DIFFERENT artifact
bites.why: the ruler judges coordinate FORMAT + linear proximity only; it cannot tell whether the 40-hex actually coordinates THIS claim. A decoy blob from another receipt satisfies the window check
bites.severity: real hole - this is the exact shape the commander predicted
bites.fix: require the durable coordinate to be on the SAME LINE as the claim, or within a much tighter window (e.g. 40 chars), or preceded by an attribution cue (出处/来源/@) on the same line

bites.class: window borrow (BIT, same root as B5)
bites.vector: two relay sentences in one block, one coordinate between them
bites.why: both claims sit within 200 chars of the same 40-hex and both pass, even though the coordinate was published for the FIRST claim's section; window borrowing across section boundaries
bites.severity: real hole - same root as B5

clean_vectors.measured: fences are invisible to the scan; still judged (RED without coord, CLEAN with) - the fence neither hides nor saves a claim

scope_limits_not_holes.what: a well-formed but NONEXISTENT file:line coordinate passes
scope_limits_not_holes.why not a hole: the ruler is a FORMAT gate; existence checking is a different instrument (the coordinate audit). Fail-open on truth, fail-closed on format - document, don't fix here

bites: B3 relay-word list is closable by rephrasing (structural coverage gap)
B5 decoy 40-hex satisfies the window (attribution hole)
B6 linear window borrowing across sections
fixes_suggested: invert F2: require a coordinate for ANY sentence with a number + attribution structure, or require same-line coordinates (B3/B5/B6 share one root: format+proximity cannot prove attribution)
the durable fix for B5/B6 is a tighter window or same-line requirement; the structural fix is attribution-cue matching
